study.title: John 17 - The priestly prayer of Jesus
study.overview: John 17 records the longest prayer of Jesus, made to the Father at the end of the farewell speech. The chapter is divided into three movements: Jesus prays for himself, for the disciples present and, finally, for all who will believe through their message. Prayer shows that the cross is not accident, but part of the Son's mission; it also shows that eternal life consists in knowing the Father and the Son, that the disciples belong to God, must be kept in the world, sanctified by the truth and led to unity. The climax of the chapter is that the love with which the Father loves the Son reaches the followers of Jesus and remains in them.

outline.title: Jesus asks the Father for glorification
outline.explanation: Jesus opens the prayer by asking the Father to glorify him, not for self-promotion, but for his work to reveal the glory of the Father himself. He defines eternal life as knowing the one true God and Jesus Christ sent by Him, and states that he has done the work received, asking for the restoration of the glory he had before creation.

outline.title: The revelation of the Father's name and the identity of the disciples
outline.explanation: Jesus says that he revealed the name of God to those whom the Father gave him, and that they received the words given by Him. These disciples recognized that Jesus came from the Father and believed in the divine submission. The text highlights that they belong to the Father, and that the work of the Son will be recognized in them.

outline.title: Protection, joy, sanctification and sending
outline.explanation: Jesus asks that the disciples be kept in the name of God, preserved by the evil one, united and full of his joy. The world hates them because they do not belong to the world, so Jesus does not withdraw them from it, but sanctifies them in the truth. He also sends them to the world as he was sent, and consecrates himself so that they may be sanctified in truth.

outline.title: Prayer for all future believers
outline.explanation: Jesus extends his intercession to those who will still believe through the word of the apostles. His central request is the visible unity among believers, reflecting the communion between the Father and the Son, so that the world may believe in the sending of Jesus. The ultimate goal is for the disciples to be with Christ and see his glory, while the Father's love remains in them through the presence of Jesus.

study.context: Notes indicate that this chapter closes the farewell speech that was previously started. Prayer is presented as Jesus" answer after speaking to the disciples, as a prayer made in an audible voice for them to hear. Adam Clarke notes that Jesus still headed toward Gethsemane, although this is an inference of the commentary and not a direct statement of the chapter. Matthew Henry points out that this is a unique prayer of Christ as Mediator, model of intercession, and not the same prayer He taught to the disciples.
study.theology: The chapter reveals a high Christology: Jesus participates in the glory before creation, received authority over all mankind, and can grant eternal life. Eternal life is defined not only as an endless duration, but as personal knowledge of the Father and the Son. There is also a strong ecclesiology: the disciples belong to the Father, receive the word of Christ, are preserved, sanctified and sent to the world. Sanctification is linked to the truth of the word of God, and not the isolation of the world; Jesus asks for protection in the midst of the world, not withdrawing from it. Christian unity is presented as a missionary witness, so that the world may believe. Finally, the chapter shows the continuous intercession of Christ and his intention to bring his to communion with him and to the participation of his glory, always as a gift of the Father and the fruit of divine love.

scholarViews.insight: Jesus opened his prayer at the end of the farewell speech, turning from what he spoke to the disciples to speak to the Father for them; this shows prayer as intercession after teaching.
Jesus distinguishes the world from the group that the Father has given him: there is a sphere of people by whom He does not pray here, in contrast to the elect given to Christ from among the world.
Jesus consecrates himself to death to buy the eternal salvation of the disciples; his sanctification is linked to the redemptive sacrifice and work.

questions: What does it mean, in practice, to know God and Jesus Christ as eternal life, and not just know things about them?
How can the church seek unity without abandoning the truth or sanctification by the word of God?
How does Jesus" prayer correct the tendency to want to be taken from the world rather than to be kept and sent within it?
study.practice: Seset time to pray for those who teach faith, new believers and those who will still believe through the testimony of the church. Ask not only external protection, but sanctification by truth, real unity, and fidelity to mission. Also examine if your way of living in public shows that you belong to God and not the world around you.
study.uncertainty: The chapter does not inform scenario details with historical precision; the idea that Jesus walked toward Gethsemane comes from an interpretative note, not from the text of John 17. The readings of the commentators are presented as interpretations and may diverge from each other. The expression "name" of God is understood here, based on the notes, as a revelation of the very character and divine truth, without extrapolating to unproven technical definitions.
